comparison.objective: Open a locker while controlling a leaning case, then extract and stand it upright; candidate rejects open loaded cartons from a belt.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-951 tests anticipatory support during door opening and upright extraction of an unstable case. Candidate tests synchronized belt tracking, low sidewall grasp under flaps and level transport preserving loose contents.
comparison.success_condition: PR-951 requires the case never exceed 45 degrees or a 0.45 m/s downward speed and finish upright, released and stable on a mat. Candidate explicitly monitors content escape, complete belt clearance, tray containment and closed-carton noncontact.
comparison.reason: There is some shared careful-container transport, but the defining abilities—supporting a door-obstructing unstable case versus intercepting an articulated loaded carton in motion—are materially different. PR-951's 20 Hz velocity sampling leaves short-drop coverage imperfect but does not create ambiguity about distinction.
